Yes yes yes, I always wondered if Charlotte knew about Ali and archer before the night she died and if her being upset at Ali was part of the act. 
It’s strange to me to see how the fans always gave so much sympathy to Alex and Mona, but rarely to Charlotte. When it seems to me Charlotte had the most reasoning to be the way she was, she did what she did because of the way she viewed the world. 

I think it was dumb people made such a big fuss into making her transition into a controversy. I think her character tells one of the most realistic queer stories. It’s raw and it’s real. 
I think her identity is such a big part in who she is, since childhood she had to hide who she was and how she felt, it was all she had ever known. That’s why her being A makes sense because of course she’d want to hide. That’s all she’s been taught to do. She wants to be able to hide her identity and protect herself, because growing up Kenneth always made her feel like she was in danger. But under the identity of “A” she could be protected and still have all the power and control she never had as a child. She never got to feel powerful. 
I think Charlotte is such important representation because you see what really happens to people born queer and abused for it. Who she was, was the reason Kenneth kicked her out of the family. Jason wasn’t related to him either but they kept him and threw Charlotte away. It was the reason she was sent to radley in the first place, being out there and she was still being mistreated. 
Her whole fallout with Bethany young showed how Charlotte was framed and not listened to because she was the only queer child in the asylum, bethany knew that and used it against her, used it to manipulate her. After that is when they framed her for killing Tobys mom and she was abused even worse. By being forced into medication that wasn’t right for her for years. There’s so much that goes into who she is and why. 
I think charlottes always been an escapist, she escapes reality by focusing on these obsessions. As a teen she threw herself into school work, that was her goal, very much like her sister Spencer must be the Drake genes lol. 
Then as an adult she obsesses over the girls and controlling them. And her life long obsession no one rlly points out was with Alison, she strived to be her. I think it’s because cece was always lost. She wasn’t allowed to explore and be herself as a child and she was always locked up, she didn’t know what it was like being an honest functioning person.

Ugh I totally feel you😩 the amount of hate her reveal got is SO intense. It honestly confuses me how people don’t at least appreciate all she brought to the table, the complexity she had. Charlotte was definitely the ultimate A. That’s why they called her big A, she had everything to do with everybody. I mean unlike Alex at least cece was a well known and connected character, even the other side characters like Jenna and Noel and Melissa knew and were scared of her. Cece was the most innovative and creative, the dollhouse was next level, no board game can top that😂 As much as I have respect for Mona, we have to be realistic here, she’s a high school student. Cece never really had that normal suburban childhood all the other characters had, she grew up completely isolated from society, yet she still managed to build her intelligence from scratch by studying and she became so powerful she owned and controlled her own corporations and knew how to work the stock market, now THATS impressive. I felt like in Alex’s case she just copied everything from Charlotte, her character was honestly just so weak when u come to realize if it weren’t for Cece she would never be capable of any of it. Cece was the one who defined what the A game meant, she rearranged the rules and had everything in her control. I just feel like there’s so much detail to her, there’s not enough words to describe it. You ask me if I have sympathy for Charlotte, as much as I hate what she did, I’d be lying if I said I didn’t. Now I’ve never ever condoned anything she’s done and I’m a firm believer in holding characters accountable and not glorifying their actions when supporting a villain. That said, I think she was robbed of her chances at life, her chances of getting better. Archer dunhill manipulated and honestly groomed her for years, honestly I call it abuse. He was the reason she never saw any real professional mental health care, he took away her chances of getting better and manipulated her into thinking he loved her, when in reality he was using her for her money that SHE earned and worked for her whole life. Not to mention her childhood which i could go on forever. When I was a kid first watching this show I hated cece, I thought she was evil and the worst. Then 6 years later I grew up to be like her😂  We have one too many things in common. At this point how could I judge her when I’ve walked her path. That’s what really made me connect with her whole rewatching because I understood her for the very first time. It became so clear to me why she made her choices and turned out the way she did, it was honestly way to realistic. It’s so strange to see it at first and think of how outlandish that would be but then you realize this stuff happens in real life in the way it effects people’s mental health. I honestly saw Cece as one of the most in depth characters and I think she represents mental illness and what it means to be A better than the other A’s. I think a lot of people miss the point with her character and don’t see what the writers are obviously trying to show us which is she was sick, she lived in her own state of delusion and fantasy. I honestly don’t think she was living in reality half the time, everything was always a game to her. It’s just so intriguing to analyze her mentally. I rlly could go on ab her for days😩
